# CHANGELOG.md
Its entries dated before 2026-10-12 stand, whole and unchanged, in `docs/archive/CHANGELOG-to-2026-10-11.md`, read with this file as one record.

The prior text of every clean edit to a spec. `changelog-reconciles` reads the git history and fails any commit that deleted a line from a spec without changing this file.

Specs are `CLAUDE.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.html`, `SCHEMA.md`, `BUILD_PLAN.md` and `RUNBOOK.md`, and the four files under `.claude/rules/`, which carry `CLAUDE.md`'s own text and are edited on the same terms. Records correct themselves with new dated entries and do not appear here.

Nothing in the corpus is struck through. A spec is edited cleanly and what it said before is written down here, with the decision that authorised the change or the defect it repairs.

## Entry format

```
### YYYY-MM-DD - <file> - <what changed>
Authorised by: <a decision name, cited exactly>   OR
Corrects: <the defect, in one line, and how it was found>
Was:
> the prior text, verbatim
Now:
> the replacing text, or a note that the passage was removed
Why: one or two sentences
```

An entry names one or the other and never neither. A change that alters what the corpus decides cites the decision that authorises it; a change that repairs a spec which was wrong when written names the defect, because there was no decision to make and inventing one to fill the field would make the field unreadable.

### 2026-10-28 - docs/RUNBOOK.md - the labeller labels on the local model under its pin, and every stored story is labelled once in batches
Authorised by: The news labeller is a process of its own the off-peak run starts, and labels on the local model under a pin of its own
Was:
> "The off-peak run starts the labeller before the drain, five minutes after each peak window ends, over the newest night's list, as a process of its own on main's clean build, so every call and every dollar it makes sits on its own run and never the night's (see: The news labeller is a process of its own the off-peak run starts, and its calls and its spend are its own); the night starts none. It is also run by hand, which is how a night whose labeller stopped at a limit is finished early, or a night's list labelled under a profile just switched to:"
> "... and for each name asks the news job's profile for a label of each of its own stored admitted articles ... Before it asks anything it resolves the profile, so a missing key stops it with its line, and asks the provider for its model list, which bills nothing, so a model that does not answer stops it there; neither falls back to another profile. Where a peak window of its profile is open before a call, it waits for the window to end, as the drain does, and then asks, so a labeller started by hand at half past one labels from four (see: The news labeller waits for the end of a peak window rather than stopping at one, and its time limit counts the time it labels). It stops at its own time limit, counted over the time it labels and not the time it waits, at its month limit and at the day or month cap, and what is left waits for the next night. It prints how many names it reached, the labels written, the unreadable answers, the articles refused by admissibility and the ones labelled before, what the run cost and the month so far, and what stopped it."
> "**A label is never overwritten** (see: ...). A label is kept by the profile that wrote it and the instruction's version, so switching the news job's profile, the one word `EquityBrief:Models:News:Use`, takes effect on the next night or the next run by hand and writes rows of its own beside the first profile's; nothing is labelled again under the old one. The shipped word is `claude-haiku`, whose provider publishes a retirement date of 2026-10-15 at the earliest, which the run page warns of from thirty days before; on the day the model stops answering the labeller stops with its line, and the fix is the one word."
Now:
> "The off-peak run starts the labeller before the drain, five minutes after each peak window ends, over the newest night's list and the names a report is written for, as a process of its own on main's clean build, so every call it makes sits on its own run and never the night's, every one of them on the local model and none paid (see: The news labeller is a process of its own the off-peak run starts, and labels on the local model under a pin of its own); the night starts none. It is also run by hand, which is how a night whose labeller stopped at a limit is finished early:"
> "... and for each name asks the local model, the local profile the settings flag as the default, for a label of each of its own stored admitted articles ... Before it asks anything it holds the run to the newest label pin, labelling nothing where none is written or where the model, its file, the instruction's version or the window differs from it, its row saying which; then it takes the local model's lock, waiting for the local run, its history read or a comparison to end rather than overlapping them, to its time limit and no further, so the drain after it is never held up past it, and loads the model where it is not loaded (see: The news labeller waits for the local model's lock and stops before the local run's next slot, its time limit counted from its start). Each answer is held by the runtime's structured output to the instruction's keys and directions; an empty answer or one cut off at its budget is asked once more, a story the runtime does not answer is left for the next run, and a runtime that is gone stops the run with its line. It stops at its own time limit, counted from its start with the wait for the lock inside it, before the local run's next slot at 12:05 or 21:40 UTC, and at its month limit, which on the local model reads nothing spent, and what is left waits for the next run. It prints how many names it reached, the labels written, the unreadable answers, the stories the runtime did not answer, the articles refused by admissibility and the ones labelled before, and what stopped it."
> two new paragraphs: `label-news --pin`, which writes the label pin by hand, and `label-news --all --until yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mmZ`, which labels every stored story once in batches stopping before the next writer's slot
> "**A label is never overwritten** (see: ...). A label is kept by the profile that wrote it and the instruction's version, so the local profile's labels stand beside the paid profile's written before the labeller moved to the local model, and nothing is labelled again under the old one; a page draws the label written under the newest instruction, the local model's where one stands. The labeller asks no paid profile and none answers in the local model's place: `EquityBrief:Models:News:Use` names the paid profile whose stored labels `compare-labels` reads, and the labeller reads it for nothing."
Why: the ruling moves the labeller to the local model, adds its pin and the batch that labels every stored story once, and the runbook states the commands; the paid profile's word and its retirement date no longer bound the labeller.

Now:
